UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile, storing personalized settings, preferences, and feature enablement flags for assistAI. Does not store authentication credentials.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

externalAuthId.description: Reference to the unique identifier from an external authentication system. (Relationship: ExternalAuthSystem 1:1 UserProfile)

preferredLanguage.description: The user's preferred language for interacting with assistAI (e.g., 'en', 'hi', 'hinglish').

personalityMode.description: The selected personality mode for the AI (e.g., 'Professional', 'Friendly', 'Casual').

isVoiceAuthEnabled.description: Flag indicating if voice authentication is enabled for this user.

isFaceUnlockEnabled.description: Flag indicating if face unlock is enabled for this user.

isCameraAccessGranted.description: Flag indicating if the user has granted camera access to the assistAI application.

isVisualRecognitionEnabled.description: Flag indicating if the visual recognition feature is enabled for this user.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was last updated.

CommandLog.title: CommandLog
CommandLog.description: Records the history of voice commands issued by a user and the actions performed by assistAI.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CommandLog entry.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who issued the command. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N CommandLog)

commandText.description: The raw transcribed voice command from the user.

interpretedIntent.description: The AI's determined intent of the command (e.g., 'openApp', 'setVolume', 'sendMessage').

extractedEntities.description: A JSON string containing key-value pairs of entities extracted from the command (e.g., '{"appName": "Chrome"}', '{"volumeLevel": 50}').

actionPerformed.description: A descriptive string of the action assistAI took in response to the command (e.g., 'Opened Google Chrome', 'Volume set to 50%').

timestamp.description: The timestamp when the command was processed.

status.description: The execution status of the command (e.g., 'Success', 'Failed', 'PendingConfirmation').

responseGiven.description: The verbal or textual response provided by assistAI to the user.

SmartDevice.title: SmartDevice
SmartDevice.description: Stores details and configuration for smart home devices integrated with assistAI.

id.description: Unique identifier for the SmartDevice entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who owns this smart device. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N SmartDevice)

name.description: A user-friendly name for the smart device (e.g., 'Living Room Light', 'Bedroom AC').

type.description: The type of smart device (e.g., 'Smart Bulb', 'Smart Plug', 'AC', 'TV').

protocol.description: The communication protocol or platform used for this device (e.g., 'MQTT', 'Google Home', 'Alexa', 'Home Assistant').

connectionDetails.description: A JSON string containing specific connection parameters or identifiers for the device (e.g., IP address, device ID, API key reference). Sensitive data should be handled securely external to this model.

status.description: The current operational status of the device (e.g., 'Online', 'Offline', 'Error').

lastKnownState.description: A JSON string representing the last known state of the device (e.g., '{"power": "on", "brightness": 80, "color": "#FFFFFF"}').

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the smart device was added.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the smart device details were last updated or its state changed.

Automation.title: Automation
Automation.description: Defines a user-created workflow macro, allowing multiple actions to be triggered by a single command.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Automation entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who created this automation. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Automation)

name.description: A user-friendly name for the automation (e.g., 'Start Work Mode', 'Good Morning Routine').

description.description: A brief description of what the automation does.

triggerPhrase.description: The specific voice command or phrase that triggers this automation.

isActive.description: Indicates if the automation is currently active and can be triggered.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the automation was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the automation was last updated.

AutomationAction.title: AutomationAction
AutomationAction.description: Represents a single step or action within a larger user-defined automation workflow.

id.description: Unique identifier for the AutomationAction entity.

automationId.description: Reference to the Automation this action belongs to. (Relationship: Automation 1:N AutomationAction)

order.description: The sequential order of this action within its automation.

actionType.description: The type of action to perform (e.g., 'openApp', 'setVolume', 'sendNotification', 'controlSmartDevice').

actionParameters.description: A JSON string containing specific parameters required for the action (e.g., '{"appName": "Slack"}', '{"deviceId": "device123", "command": "turnOn", "value": "on"}').

description.description: A brief description of this specific action (e.g., 'Open Slack', 'Turn on living room light').

Reminder.title: Reminder
Reminder.description: Stores user-set reminders for productivity and task management.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Reminder entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who created this reminder. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Reminder)

message.description: The message or content of the reminder (e.g., 'Take a 15-minute break', 'Call mom').

scheduledTime.description: The specific date and time when the reminder is scheduled to trigger.

isRecurring.description: Flag indicating if the reminder is a recurring event.

recurrencePattern.description: A string defining the recurrence pattern for recurring reminders (e.g., 'daily', 'weekly', 'every 3 hours', 'cron-like expression').

status.description: The current status of the reminder (e.g., 'Pending', 'Completed', 'Dismissed').

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the reminder was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the reminder was last updated.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed following a user-centric, path-based ownership model to ensure strong security, scalability, and debuggability. All user-specific data is nested under a top-level `/users/{userId}` collection, where `{userId}` directly corresponds to the authenticated Firebase `request.auth.uid`.

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):**
1.  **User Profiles (`/users/{userId}`):** The `UserProfile` document itself is stored at `/users/{userId}`. Access to this document is controlled by ensuring `request.auth.uid == userId` from the path. The `externalAuthId` field within the `UserProfile` document will store the `uid`, implicitly making the document self-referential for authorization without requiring any `get()` calls.
2.  **Subcollections (`/users/{userId}/command_logs`, `/users/{userId}/smart_devices`, `/users/{userId}/automations`, `/users/{userId}/reminders`):** For all direct subcollections of a user profile, the `userId` is inherently part of the document path. This means that rules can directly compare `request.auth.uid` with the `{userId}` wildcard in the path, ensuring that only the owner can access their data. The `userId` field is also explicitly present in these documents (e.g., `CommandLog.userId`), serving as a denormalized field that *could* be used for validation but is primarily for data integrity, as the path itself provides the necessary authorization context without `get()` calls.
3.  **Nested Subcollections (`/users/{userId}/automations/{automationId}/actions`):** The `AutomationAction` entity is a subcollection of `Automation`. By nesting it under the user's path (`/users/{userId}/automations/{automationId}/actions/{actionId}`), the `userId` (owner of the automation) is available directly in the path. To further reinforce Authorization Independence, the `AutomationAction` document must also include the `userId` (denormalized from its parent `Automation` or inferred from the path) and `automationId`. This ensures that a security rule for `AutomationAction` can simply check `request.auth.uid == userId` present in the document or path, without needing a `get()` call to the parent `Automation` document.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
The structural segregation ensures that `list` operations (queries) can be secured efficiently. Since all documents within any user-specific collection (e.g., `/users/{userId}/command_logs`) inherently belong to the `userId` specified in the path, a query like `db.collection('users/{userId}/command_logs').where('timestamp', '>', someTime)` is inherently constrained by `request.auth.uid == userId`. This means that users can only query their *own* data, satisfying the Queryability by Authorization Principle without requiring complex server-side filtering or inefficient security rules that attempt to filter on document content after retrieval. The consistent use of `userId` in the path and within documents allows for straightforward, efficient security rules for both `get` and `list` operations.

**Structural Segregation & Access Modeling:**
All data is kept private to the user. There are no 'public' collections mixed with 'private' data, simplifying security rules immensely. The `DBAC` principle is implicitly handled as all authorization is based on `request.auth.uid` and path-based ownership, with no custom claims or global roles defined in this structure. This design strongly adheres to the core principles for a secure, scalable, and debuggable Firestore implementation.
